label: Laboratory Information Management
retrieval_text: Laboratory Information Management. LIMS. The domain of systems and processes that manage the full lifecycle of samples, tests, and results in an analytical, clinical, environmental, or quality-control laboratory. A laboratory information management system governs the receipt, accessioning, aliquoting, storage under controlled conditions, and disposal of specimens; the ordering, scheduling, and execution of assays and analytical methods on instruments; the capture, validation, and interpretation of measured results — values with units and measurement uncertainty — against specification limits and reference ranges; the flagging of exceedances and out-of-specification outcomes; chain-of-custody and provenance tracking across every transfer; and quality control, instrument calibration, and regulatory compliance. It coordinates specimens and aliquots, service requests (test orders), observations and diagnostic reports (results), devices and instruments, reagents and substances, analytical methods and protocols, and the technicians, study directors, and organizations responsible for each step.. Covers analytical, clinical, environmental-monitoring, biobank, and quality-control laboratories operating under GxP, ISO/IEC 17025, CLIA, or OECD test-guideline regimes. The governed entities map onto FHIR diagnostics resources (Specimen, ServiceRequest, Observation, DiagnosticReport, Device, Substance) and onto a SysML systems view in which the laboratory is a system whose sample lifecycle, instrument allocations, and acceptance constraints are first-class.. Sample receipt, accessioning, testing, result review, reporting, and archival; analyte measurement; turnaround and throughput; accreditation and audit.

label: Specimen Lifecycle Management
retrieval_text: Specimen Lifecycle Management. LIMS_SPECIMEN_LIFECYCLE. The governed progression of a physical specimen through its laboratory states: collection from a subject or source, receipt and accessioning under a unique identifier, partitioning into aliquots, storage at a controlled location and temperature, assignment to testing, and finally reporting, retention, and disposal. Each state transition is an event with a timestamp, an actor, and a chain-of-custody record establishing unbroken provenance; specimens carry collection method, body site or sampling point, container and preservative, volume, and condition-on-receipt. This is the sample-lifecycle finite-state machine at the heart of a laboratory: received → accessioned → aliquoted → tested → reported → archived or destroyed.. Includes aliquot derivation and parent-child specimen relationships, freezer and storage-location management, stability and expiry, and custody transfers between collection site, transport, and testing laboratory. Corresponds to FHIR Specimen and its collection, processing, and container backbone.

label: Energy and Well Drilling
retrieval_text: Energy and Well Drilling. ENERGY. The upstream energy domain of drilling, logging, and operating wells to access subsurface hydrocarbons. A well is a constructed feature whose wellbore is drilled along a planned trajectory through geological formations; the operation is instrumented by well logs and downhole measurement, recorded as channels and mud logs, and surveyed as trajectory stations. Drilling is executed by a rig running a bottom-hole assembly with a bit on tubulars, supported by cementing, casing, and well-stimulation operations, and documented in drilling and operations reports. This is the WITSML systems view of well construction and data transfer.. Covers well planning, directional drilling, well logging and petrophysics, mud logging, casing and completion, and drilling operations. Maps onto the WITSML 2.0 data model (Well, Wellbore, Trajectory, Log, Channel, MudLog, Rig, BhaRun, Tubular, DrillReport) and the Energistics transfer protocol.. Wells, wellbores, drilling, logging, trajectory survey, mud, rig and bottom-hole assembly, casing, formation evaluation.

label: Wells, Wellbores and Subsurface Targets
retrieval_text: Wells, Wellbores and Subsurface Targets. ENERGY_WELLBORE. The constructed subsurface features of a drilling project. A well is the facility that accesses a subsurface target; a wellbore is the drilled hole within it, with an as-built geometry of hole sizes, casing strings, and cement. Wells are planned to reach geological targets at depth, drilled in sections, and cased and completed to produce or inject fluids. Each wellbore records its geometry, the formations it penetrates, and the casing and completion that line it.. Includes hole sections, casing and tubing strings, completions, and subsurface targets. Corresponds to WITSML Well, Wellbore, WellboreGeometry, and Target.

label: Well Logging and Downhole Measurement
retrieval_text: Well Logging and Downhole Measurement. ENERGY_LOGGING. The measurement of subsurface properties along a wellbore and the records it produces. A well log is a record of one or more measurement channels indexed by depth or time; a mud log records formation and cuttings observations made while drilling; formation markers pick the boundaries of geological units. Logging quantifies petrophysical properties — porosity, resistivity, gamma, density — through wireline and measurement-while-drilling tools, and the resulting channels and channel-sets are the primary evidence for formation evaluation.. Includes wireline and measurement-while-drilling logs, channel sets, petrophysical curves, mud logs, and formation tops. Corresponds to WITSML Log, WellLog, ChannelSet, Channel, MudLog, and FormationMarker.

label: Wellbore Trajectory and Survey
retrieval_text: Wellbore Trajectory and Survey. ENERGY_TRAJECTORY. The geometric path of a wellbore through space and its measurement. A trajectory is the three-dimensional path the wellbore follows from surface to target; trajectory stations are surveyed points along it, each recording measured depth, inclination, and azimuth from which position is computed. Directional drilling steers the wellbore along a planned trajectory to hit subsurface targets while honouring dogleg and anti-collision constraints, and the survey program defines how and where the path is measured.. Includes directional plans, survey stations, minimum-curvature position computation, dogleg severity, and anti-collision. Corresponds to WITSML Trajectory, TrajectoryStation, and SurveyProgram.

label: Drilling Operations and Rig Equipment
retrieval_text: Drilling Operations and Rig Equipment. ENERGY_OPERATIONS. The operations and equipment that drill and service a well. A rig is the equipment assembly that drills the well, running a bottom-hole assembly with a bit on a string of tubulars; operations include drilling ahead, tripping, cementing, and well stimulation, each recorded against a plan in drilling and operations reports. Equipment, fluids, time breakdown, and operational risks are logged so that performance and non-productive time can be analysed and the next operation planned.. Includes bottom-hole-assembly runs, bits and tubulars, cementing and stimulation jobs, daily drilling reports, fluids reports, and risk logs. Corresponds to WITSML Rig, BhaRun, Tubular, Bit, CementJob, StimJob, DrillReport, FluidsReport, and Risk.

label: Solid Geometry Design for Consumer Electronics
retrieval_text: Solid Geometry Design for Consumer Electronics. CSG. The domain of designing the three-dimensional solid geometry of consumer-electronics products and preparing it for fabrication. Constructive solid geometry builds an enclosure, chassis, heat sink, or bracket as a boolean tree over primitive solids — blocks, cylinders, cones, tori, and arbitrary polyhedra — combined by union, intersection, and difference into regions and combinations; boundary representations (meshes, NURBS, n-manifold geometry) and sketch-extrude-revolve construction give the curved housings, button and display apertures, connector openings, snap-fit and boss features, ribs, and thermal cutouts of an electronic product. The geometry is designed against the electronics it packages — board outlines and keep-outs, connector envelopes, antenna windows, thermal paths — and against the process that will fabricate it. This is the BRL-CAD solid-modeling view applied to electronics product design: primitives, the CSG boolean tree, and boundary representations, in the service of devices that must be molded, formed, machined, and assembled.. Covers enclosure and housing design for phones, wearables, network equipment, and lab instruments; chassis, frames, heat sinks, light pipes, gaskets, and fastening features; PCB outline and keep-out geometry; design-for-manufacture of molded and formed parts. Maps onto the BRL-CAD primitive set (arb8, sph, ell, tor, tgc, bot, nmg, brep, bspline, superell) and CSG combination machinery (regions, combinations, boolean union/intersection/difference), and onto the SysML v2 geometry library (shape and spatial items).. Enclosures, housings, heat sinks, snap-fits, bosses and ribs, board keep-outs; solid primitives, boolean CSG, boundary representation; design for molding and forming.

label: Solid Primitives and Shapes
retrieval_text: Solid Primitives and Shapes. CSG_PRIMITIVE. The basic solid building blocks of constructive solid geometry. A primitive is a parametric solid shape with a closed-form boundary: spheres and ellipsoids, tori, truncated general cones and elliptical cylinders, arbitrary convex polyhedra, superellipsoids, hyperboloids, and particles. Each primitive is defined by a handful of parameters — radii, vertices, axes — and occupies a spatial region; primitives are the leaves of the CSG boolean tree from which compound solids are built.. Includes the canonical solid primitives and their parameters. Corresponds to the BRL-CAD primitives arb8/arbn/sph/ell/tor/tgc/rec/rhc/rpc/ehy/epa/eto/superell/hyp/half/part and the SysML shape items.

label: Constructive Solid Geometry and Boolean Composition
retrieval_text: Constructive Solid Geometry and Boolean Composition. CSG_BOOLEAN. The construction of compound solids by boolean composition of primitives. Constructive solid geometry combines solids by union, intersection, and difference (subtraction) into a CSG tree whose internal nodes are boolean operations and whose leaves are primitives. A region is a combination of primitives forming a solid with assigned material; a combination is a boolean tree over primitives and sub-combinations. Parametric construction sketches a two-dimensional profile and extrudes or revolves it into a solid, then composes the results into the final model.. Includes boolean union, intersection, and difference; the CSG tree; regions and combinations; and sketch-extrude-revolve construction. Corresponds to the BRL-CAD region/combination model and boolean operators, and SysML CSG examples.

label: Boundary Representation, Meshes and NURBS
retrieval_text: Boundary Representation, Meshes and NURBS. CSG_BREP. The representation of a solid by its bounding surface rather than by a boolean tree. A boundary representation describes a solid as a set of trimmed faces, edges, and vertices; n-manifold geometry and NURBS or B-spline surfaces give exact curved boundaries, while a bag-of-triangles mesh tessellates the surface into facets for display and analysis. Boundary representations interoperate with constructive solid geometry — a CSG model can be evaluated into a boundary representation, and surfaces can be combined into solids.. Includes boundary representation, n-manifold geometry, NURBS and B-spline surfaces, and polygonal meshes and tessellation. Corresponds to the BRL-CAD brep/nmg/bot/bspline primitives.

label: Design for Fabrication of Electronic Products
retrieval_text: Design for Fabrication of Electronic Products. CSG_FABRICATION. The discipline of shaping consumer-electronics geometry so it can actually be made. Design for fabrication constrains the solid model by the production process that will realize it: injection-molded housings carry draft angles, uniform wall thickness, boss and rib proportions, gate and ejector locations, and parting-line placement; sheet-metal chassis respect bend radii, relief cuts, and flat-pattern development; machined heat sinks and bezels respect tool access and fillet radii; and every mating feature carries the tolerances that make snap-fits, fasteners, and gaskets assemble. Tolerance stack-up across the enclosure, board, and connectors decides whether the device closes; the fabricated part is verified against the solid model by inspection dimensions. This is where the geometric design meets the manufacturing processes that produce it — the same molding, forming, machining, and assembly operations that manufacturing engineering plans and routes.. Includes draft, wall-thickness, boss and rib rules for injection molding; bend and relief rules for sheet metal; tolerance stack-up and fit for snap-together assemblies; inspection dimensions and first-article verification. Intersects the manufacturing-process domain (process planning, tooling, routing) — the CSG-to-manufacturing seam.

label: Assay and Method Execution
retrieval_text: Assay and Method Execution. LIMS_ASSAY_EXECUTION. The ordering, scheduling, and performance of an analytical assay or test method on a specimen using an instrument or workcell. A method consumes reagents, calibrators, and controls and produces measurements; a run reifies a protocol of ordered steps — sample and reagent addition, incubation, separation, detection — executed under defined parameters, and is allocated to a specific instrument and operator. Each assay declares its analytes, its measurement principle, its calibration model, and its acceptance criteria; a run records the instrument, lot numbers, environmental conditions, and the raw and processed signal from which results are computed.. Includes test ordering and worklist scheduling, reagent-kit and instrument-model variants, method-to-instrument allocation, and protocol or standard-operating-procedure steps. Corresponds to FHIR ServiceRequest (the order) and Device/Substance (instruments and reagents) and the SysML action and allocation views.

label: Utility-Scale Networks
retrieval_text: Utility-Scale Networks. UTILITY. The domain of engineering, operating, and maintaining utility-scale infrastructure networks: electric power transmission and distribution, water and wastewater systems, and carrier-grade telecommunications. A utility network is a system of connected assets — substations, transformers, and feeders; pumping stations, mains, and valves; central offices, fiber routes, and switching elements — whose topology carries a flow of power, fluid, or data from sources to consumers. Networks are modeled in the systems view: assets are parts bearing ports, spans and mains are connections realizing interfaces, capacity and reliability are requirements and constraints, and switching, outage response, and maintenance are the operational actions and states. Telemetry from field devices monitors flows, pressures, voltages, and traffic against operating limits, and network state — energized, pressurized, in-service, degraded — is tracked per asset and per span. This is the SysML v2 interconnection view applied at utility scale: connected parts, typed flows, allocation of service demand onto physical infrastructure, and requirement-driven operation.. Covers electric transmission and distribution, water and wastewater conveyance, and carrier telecommunications networks; network topology and asset registries; SCADA-style telemetry and operating limits; capacity planning, contingency, and outage management. Maps onto the SysML v2 systems libraries (Parts, Ports, Interfaces, Connections, Flows, Requirements, Constraints, States, Actions) and the Quantities-and-Units (ISQ/SI) domain library for flows, voltages, and pressures.. Grids, mains, and carrier networks as connected part topologies; flows and capacities; telemetry against limits; switching, outages, and maintenance operations.

label: Electric Power Transmission and Distribution
retrieval_text: Electric Power Transmission and Distribution. UTILITY_POWER. The networked delivery of electric power from generation to load. Transmission moves bulk power at high voltage between substations over lines and cables; distribution steps voltage down through transformers and carries it along feeders, laterals, and service drops to customers. Substations compose transformers, buses, breakers, switches, and protection relays into switching topologies; grid operation balances load against capacity, maintains voltage and frequency within limits, reconfigures the network by switching, and isolates faults through protection coordination. Asset registries record each transformer, breaker, and line span with its ratings, age, and condition; telemetry streams voltages, currents, and breaker states against operating limits; and contingency analysis asks whether the network survives the loss of any single element.. Includes substations, transformers, feeders and laterals, protection and switching, load and capacity ratings, voltage regulation, outage and reliability indices, and grid telemetry. The network is a connected-part topology with typed electrical flows in the systems view.

label: Water and Wastewater Networks
retrieval_text: Water and Wastewater Networks. UTILITY_WATER. The networked conveyance of potable water from sources to consumers and of wastewater from consumers to treatment. A distribution system composes intakes, treatment works, pumping stations, storage tanks, and pressure zones connected by mains, with valves, hydrants, meters, and service connections as controllable and measurable points; a collection system gathers sewage and stormwater through gravity mains, lift stations, and interceptors to treatment plants. Hydraulic behaviour — flows, pressures, and levels — is monitored against operating bands; pumps and valves are the actuated elements that move the system between states; and asset condition, leakage, and main breaks drive maintenance and renewal programs. Water quality is sampled and tested along the network, tying the utility domain to laboratory analysis.. Includes pumping stations, pressure zones, storage, mains and valves, metering, leakage and non-revenue water, lift stations and interceptors, and hydraulic telemetry. Water-quality sampling and testing intersect the laboratory domain — the utility-to-LIMS seam.

label: Carrier-Grade Telecommunications Networks
retrieval_text: Carrier-Grade Telecommunications Networks. UTILITY_TELECOM. The networked delivery of communications service at carrier scale. A carrier network composes central offices, points of presence, and data centers connected by fiber routes, conduits, and microwave links, with switching, routing, and transport elements — network equipment as engineered hardware — terminating and cross-connecting circuits and packet flows. Network elements expose ports; spans and cross-connects realize connections; aggregation, ring, and mesh topologies provide capacity and survivability; and service provisioning allocates customer demand onto physical paths. Operations monitor traffic, loss, and latency against service objectives, manage faults and protection switchover, and track every element, card, port, and fiber strand in inventory with its location, state, and connectivity — the physical-network record from which the network is operated and grown.. Includes central offices and points of presence, fiber-plant and conduit records, switching and routing elements, transport and aggregation topologies, circuit and service provisioning, network inventory, and performance and fault management. The equipment itself is manufactured electronics — the utility-to-manufacturing seam.

label: Data Engineering, Metadata and Lineage
retrieval_text: Data Engineering, Metadata and Lineage. DATAENG. The domain of systems and practices that organize, describe, move, and govern structured data across its lifecycle. A data platform ingests records from source systems into datasets — tables, files, and streams — modeled as relations of typed columns bound by primary and foreign keys, normalized to reduce redundancy or deliberately denormalized for query performance, and sometimes generalized into entity-attribute-value structures where attributes are data rather than schema. Transformations move and reshape data from source datasets to derived ones, and the record of which job run read which inputs and wrote which outputs is the data's lineage. A metadata catalog describes every dataset and column with business glossary terms, semantic types, classifications, ownership, and sensitivity, so that a bare column name and its values can be annotated with the concept it represents. Data quality is profiled and constrained: cardinality, null rates, value distributions, uniqueness, and referential integrity are measured against expectations, and violations are surfaced as observability signals. This domain is reflexive — it is the domain of describing data itself, and its own artifacts (schemas, lineage graphs, catalogs, profiles) are the structured records it governs.. Spans relational and dimensional modeling, entity-attribute-value and semi-structured designs, ETL and ELT transformation, data lineage and provenance (OpenLineage-style dataset/job/run facets), metadata catalogs and business glossaries, semantic-type and property annotation of columns (column type and column property annotation), data profiling and quality, and referential-integrity and constraint management. It is the horizontal domain beneath every vertical: laboratory results, manufacturing bills of material, well logs, and network inventories all land as datasets whose columns want semantic description.. Datasets, columns, keys, EAV; lineage and provenance; catalogs, glossaries, semantic types; profiling, quality, constraints. The domain of data describing data.

label: Relational and Schema Modeling
retrieval_text: Relational and Schema Modeling. DATAENG_MODELING. The design of structured schemas that represent a domain as related tables of typed columns. An entity becomes a table; its attributes become columns with datatypes, nullability, and value domains; its identity becomes a primary key — a natural key drawn from real-world identifiers or a surrogate key minted by the system; and its relationships to other entities become foreign keys that reference those keys. Normalization decomposes tables to eliminate update anomalies — first normal form removing repeating groups, second and third removing partial and transitive dependencies, Boyce-Codd tightening the key discipline — while dimensional and denormalized designs deliberately trade redundancy for read performance in analytical stars and snowflakes. Where attributes are too many, too sparse, or too variable to model as fixed columns, an entity-attribute-value design stores them as rows — an attribute name, a value, and the entity they describe — trading queryability for flexibility. The modeling choices determine what can be asked of the data and how faithfully the schema mirrors the domain it encodes.. Includes primary and foreign keys, natural versus surrogate keys, composite keys, normalization through Boyce-Codd normal form, star and snowflake dimensional designs, entity-attribute-value and wide-sparse tables, datatypes and value domains, and referential integrity. The schema shapes here are what a relational corpus must exhibit to be structurally realistic.

label: Data Lineage and Provenance
retrieval_text: Data Lineage and Provenance. DATAENG_LINEAGE. The recorded account of how data came to be — which processes read which inputs and produced which outputs, and how a given field's value can be traced back through every transformation to its origin. A lineage graph relates datasets as nodes and the job runs that transform them as edges: a run of a job consumes input datasets, applies a transformation, and emits output datasets, each carrying facets that describe its schema, statistics, and version at that moment. Column-level lineage refines this to the field, recording that an output column was computed from specific input columns by a named expression, so that the provenance of any value is a path through the graph. Provenance answers questions of trust and impact: whether a figure can be relied upon given its sources, what downstream artifacts must change when an upstream schema changes, and where an error was introduced. It is the substrate of reproducibility — a run is fully determined by its inputs, its transformation, and its code, and the lineage record is the standing evidence of that determination.. Includes dataset-job-run models (OpenLineage-style), input and output facets, schema and statistics facets, dataset and run versioning, column-level lineage, impact analysis, and reproducibility attribution across the window-strategy-code determinants of a run. Provenance is the reflexive core: the pipeline's own runs are lineage-tracked artifacts.

label: Metadata Cataloging and Semantic Annotation
retrieval_text: Metadata Cataloging and Semantic Annotation. DATAENG_CATALOG. The description of datasets and columns with the meaning, governance, and semantics that a bare schema omits. A metadata catalog inventories every dataset with its owner, description, freshness, and access policy, and describes every column with a business glossary term, a semantic type, and a classification of sensitivity. The central inference is semantic annotation: given only a column's name and a sample of its values, determine the concept it represents — column type annotation assigns each column a single semantic type from a controlled vocabulary or ontology, and column property annotation assigns the relationships a column participates in, such as being the subject identifier of a table or a measured property of an entity. A business glossary organizes these types into a hierarchy of terms with definitions, synonyms, and parent-child relationships, grounding physical columns in a shared conceptual vocabulary so that the same real-world concept is recognized across differently-named columns in different schemas. The catalog is what turns a warehouse of opaque tables into a queryable, governed, semantically-described asset.. Includes data catalogs, business glossaries and controlled vocabularies, semantic types and reference categories, column type annotation and column property annotation, ownership and stewardship, sensitivity and data classification, and the grounding of physical columns in a conceptual vocabulary. This is the domain the blind-column-classification task operates in — the annotation of columns against an ontology.

label: Data Profiling, Quality and Observability
retrieval_text: Data Profiling, Quality and Observability. DATAENG_QUALITY. The measurement of data against expectations of correctness, completeness, and consistency, and the surfacing of deviations as actionable signals. Profiling computes the empirical shape of a column — its cardinality and distinct-value count, null and blank rates, minimum and maximum, value-length and numeric distributions, and the patterns its values match — from which a semantic type and a value domain can be inferred and against which drift can be detected. Quality rules assert expectations: that a key is unique, that a foreign key resolves, that a value falls within a permissible set or numeric band, that a not-null column is populated, that a distribution stays within historical bounds; violations are counted, scored, and routed. Observability lifts these measures to the pipeline level — freshness, volume, schema-change, and distribution monitors watch datasets over time and raise anomalies when a table arrives late, changes shape, or shifts its statistics, closing the loop between how data is described and whether it remains true to that description.. Includes column profiling (cardinality, null rates, distributions, patterns), value-domain and semantic-type inference from values, quality rules and expectations, uniqueness and referential-integrity checks, constraint validation, and data observability (freshness, volume, schema, and distribution monitors). Profiling statistics are the evidence a semantic annotation is tested against — the quality-to-catalog seam.

label: Result Capture and Interpretation
retrieval_text: Result Capture and Interpretation. LIMS_RESULT_INTERPRETATION. The capture, validation, and clinical or regulatory interpretation of the measured outcome of an assay. A result is a quantity — a value with a unit and a measurement uncertainty — or a coded qualitative finding, attached to a specimen and an analyte, produced by a method run. Results are validated against specification limits, reference ranges, and acceptance criteria, flagged when out of specification or critical, reviewed and released by a qualified reviewer, and assembled into a diagnostic report. Interpretation compares the measured value to thresholds and prior results, derives flags and verdicts, and records the responsible reviewer and the time of release.. Includes measurement uncertainty and significant figures, reference-range and spec-limit comparison, out-of-specification handling, delta checks, result amendment, and report assembly. Corresponds to FHIR Observation (the result) and DiagnosticReport (the released report).

label: Quality, Compliance and Traceability
retrieval_text: Quality, Compliance and Traceability. LIMS_QUALITY_TRACEABILITY. The quality-management and regulatory backbone of a laboratory: quality-control samples and control charts, instrument calibration and maintenance, proficiency testing, and the end-to-end traceability that links each released result back through the method, the instrument, the reagent lots, the operator, the specimen, and the originating specification or requirement. Acceptance criteria and specification limits are enforced as parametric constraints over result columns; deviations, nonconformances, and corrective actions are recorded; and an audit trail makes every state change attributable. This is the specification → method → result traceability matrix that GxP and ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation require.. Includes control charts and Westgard-style rules, calibration verification, audit trails, deviation and CAPA management, and requirement-to-result traceability. Corresponds to the SysML requirement satisfy/verify and constraint views and to regulated-laboratory compliance regimes.

label: Manufacturing and Systems Engineering
retrieval_text: Manufacturing and Systems Engineering. MFG. The domain of designing, specifying, and producing engineered physical systems and their components. A system is decomposed into parts, assemblies, and subassemblies connected through ports and interfaces; its required capabilities are captured as requirements and constraints and checked by analysis and verification cases; and its behaviour is modeled as actions and states. Designs are realized through manufacturing processes — machining, molding, fabrication, welding, and assembly — governed by tolerances, materials, and bills of material. This is the SysML v2 systems view: parts and items bearing ports, connections, and allocations, with requirements, constraints, and quantities and units (ISQ/SI) as first-class.. Covers consumer electronics, networking and telecommunications hardware, mechanical and electromechanical assemblies, industrial equipment, and laboratory-automation hardware. Maps onto the SysML v2 standard library (Parts, Items, Ports, Interfaces, Connections, Actions, States, Requirements, Constraints, AnalysisCases) and the Quantities-and-Units (ISQ/SI) domain library.. Parts, assemblies, interfaces, requirements, tolerances, manufacturing processes, bills of material, verification.
